53	## Word timings and word style
54	
55	A caption page is a text clip with a time on each word. `set_text` edits these like any other text key. See [Edit captions](/captions/edit-captions/) and [Word caption styles](/captions/word-caption-styles/).
56	
57	### Word timings
58	
59	`words` is one `{start, end}` per whitespace-separated word of `content`, in ticks from the clip's start, or `[]` for an untimed page.
60	
61	- When the list isn't empty, it must hold exactly one timing for each word. If not, the call answers "this text is timed word by word: 5 timings for 6 words".
62	- A change to `content` that alters the word count must send `words: []` in the same patch.
63	- A word's `end` can't come before its `start`, and each `start` can't come before the one before it. Two words can start together.
64	- A negative `start` is allowed. It means the word was already being said when the clip began.
65	- The times snap to the frame grid, so two words can land on one frame.
66	
67	`words` can't be animated: `set_action_end` refuses it.
68	
69	### Word style
70	
71	`word_style` is `null` or an object. It replaces `animation` on the page.
72	
73	| Key | What it does | Values | Default |
74	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
75	| `mode` | `highlight` draws the whole page and picks out the active word. `build` makes words appear as they're said. | `highlight`, `build` | `highlight` |
76	| `active_color` | The active word's colour. | Four numbers | The text's colour |
77	| `active_scale` | Where the active word's pop settles. 1 is no pop. | 1 to 1.5 | 1 |
78	| `active_pill` | A rounded plate behind the active word. | `null`, or `{color, padding, radius, glide}` | No plate |
79	| `spoken_color` | The colour of words already said. | Four numbers | The text's colour |
80	| `upcoming_color` | The colour of words not yet said, in `highlight` mode. | Four numbers | The text's colour |
81	| `active_fill` | Fills the active word left to right as it's said. | `true`, `false` | `false` |
82	| `pause_dim` | How far the words and pill fade in a pause. | 0 to 1 | 0 |
83	
84	**The pill.** Its `padding` and `radius` are fractions of the text's `size`, starting from 0.2 and 0.25, and its `color` starts as purple. `glide` set to `true` slides the pill from the word before to the active one over 0.2 s, or sooner when the next word starts sooner, instead of jumping.
85	
86	**The fill.** `active_fill` runs from the word's start to its end, taking 0.6 s at most. The part already said draws in `active_color` and the rest in `upcoming_color`, or isn't drawn yet in `build` mode. In `highlight` mode it shows only where those two colours differ.
87	
88	**The pause dim.** `pause_dim` fades the words and the pill to 1 minus `pause_dim` of their opacity, over 0.1 s each way, in a pause of 0.25 s or more. A pause runs from one word's end to the next one's start, before a late first word, and after the last word until the clip ends.
89	
90	```json
91	{ "word_style": { "active_pill": { "glide": true }, "pause_dim": 0.5 } }
92	```
93	
94	## `set_shape`
95	
96	Changes a shape clip's geometry and paint. It mirrors the Clip tab's Shape sub-tab. See [Shape fill, stroke and size](/text-and-shapes/shape-settings/).
97	
98	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
99	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
100	| `clips` | array of integers | Yes | The shape clips to change, at least one. `get_project` lists their ids. |
101	| `patch` | object | Yes | The shape properties to change. The table below lists its keys. |
102	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest id, to edit inside that nest. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
103	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
104	
105	| Patch key | What it does | Values |
106	| --- | --- | --- |
107	| `kind` | The shape. Changing it changes only the kind. | `rectangle`, `ellipse`, `line`, `arrow` |
108	| `width`, `height` | The box, in source pixels. | Above 0 |
109	| `stroke` | The outline. `null` removes it. | `null`, or `{width, color}` |
110	| `fill` | The flat fill. `null` removes it. | `null`, or a colour |
111	| `radius` | A rectangle's corners. | 0 or more |
112	| `arrow_start`, `arrow_end` | Whether a line or arrow has a head at that end. | `true`, `false` |
113	| `from`, `to` | A line's or arrow's ends, as unit coordinates in its box. | Two numbers each, such as `[0, 1]` and `[1, 0]` |
114	| `gradient` | A gradient fill. | `null`, or `{kind, stops, angle}` |
115	
116	```json
117	{ "clips": [30], "patch": { "fill": [0.1, 0.2, 0.9, 1], "stroke": null, "radius": 24 } }
118	```
119	
120	Because changing `kind` changes only the kind, an arrow made this way keeps whatever `arrow_end` it had, unlike one created by `add_shape_clip`. See [Lines and arrows](/text-and-shapes/lines-and-arrows/).
121	
122	**Gradient.** A gradient takes precedence over `fill` while it's set and leaves `fill` in place, so `{gradient: null}` brings the flat colour back. `{gradient: {}}` starts a black-to-white ramp running left to right. See [Gradient fills](/text-and-shapes/gradients/).
123	
124	| Key | What it does | Values |
125	| --- | --- | --- |
126	| `kind` | The ramp's form. A radial gradient is an ellipse inscribed in the box. | `linear`, `radial` |
127	| `stops` | 2 to 8 `{at, color}` objects, `at` being 0 to 1 along the ramp. They needn't be sorted. Sending `stops` replaces them all. | A list |
128	| `angle` | Degrees from the right, turning counter-clockwise. It means nothing for `radial`. | Any number |
129	
130	A `line` or `arrow` has no area and ignores the gradient.
131	
132	**When it refuses.** A key the patch doesn't know, a value outside its range, or a clip that isn't a shape clip ("clip 7 has no shape properties") is an error naming what's wrong. Shapes can't be animated: an action's end has no shape group.
133	
134	## `set_clip`
135	
136	Sets a clip's name and colour label. It mirrors the timeline's inline rename, the Clip tab's name field, **Clip ▸ Rename…** (<kbd>⇧⌘R</kbd>) and **Clip ▸ Label ▸**. See [Clip names and labels](/timeline/names-and-labels/).
137	
138	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
139	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
140	| `clips` | array of integers | Yes | The clips to change, at least one. `get_project` lists their ids. |
141	| `patch` | object | Yes | `name`, `label` or both. A key left out keeps its value, and `null` clears it. |
142	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest id, to edit inside that nest. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
143	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
144	
145	```json
146	{ "clips": [12], "patch": { "name": "Intro", "label": "green" } }
147	```
148	
149	**Names.** Names are trimmed, and an empty or blank name clears the name, as `null` does. A clip with no name of its own shows what it holds: the nest, the media file, a text clip's words, or its kind.
150	
151	**Labels.** The six labels are `red`, `orange`, `yellow`, `green`, `blue` and `purple`, drawn as a dot on the clip. The label is stored as given, so keep to these names. Any other name draws in the neutral text colour.
152	
153	A split, duplicate, detach or paste carries the name and label along. `paste_attributes` never does.
154	
155	**When it refuses.** A key other than `name` or `label`, or a value that's neither a string nor `null`, is an error.
156	
157	## `text_behind_subject`
158	
159	Puts a title behind the person in a clip of a video file or a picture, in one undo step. It mirrors **Insert ▸ Text Behind Subject**. See [Text Behind Subject](/effects/text-behind-subject/).
160	
161	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
162	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
163	| `clip` | integer | No | The clip to put the title behind. Left out, it's picked at `at`. |
164	| `content` | string | No | The title's text. Left out, it's the Title preset's. |
165	| `at` | integer | No | Where the title starts, in ticks, snapped to the frame grid. Left out, it's the playhead. |
166	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
167	
168	The step does four things:
169	
170	- It adds a track named "Behind Subject" directly above the clip's track, and above any matte tracks in front of it.
171	- It adds a text clip with the Title preset at `at`, for 4 s or the rest of the clip if that's shorter.
172	- It sets `behind_subject` on the title.
173	- If the clip has no cutout yet, it sets `{cutout: {background: keep}}` on it, so the camera stays whole and the person still hides the title.
174	
175	The person's masks are made on your Mac, with no key. `analyze_cutout` says where they stand. See [Tools: reading analysis](/mcp/tools-analysis/).
176	
177	**Which clip it picks.** Without `clip`, it looks at the clips of a video file or a picture, with their video on, playing at `at`, on a shown track that isn't a matte track. It takes the front-most selected one, else the front-most with a cutout, else the front-most. The selection is left as it was.
178	
179	**What it answers.**
180	
181	| Key | What it is |
182	| --- | --- |
183	| `ok` | `true`. |
184	| `clip` | The clip the title is behind. |
185	| `track` | The new track's id. |
186	| `text` | The title's clip id. |
187	| `duration` | The title's length, in ticks. |
188	| `cutout_added` | Whether the clip was given a cutout. |
189	| `project` | The project summary. |
190	
191	**When it refuses.** Nothing is done when:
192	
193	- A nest is open. It works on the top-level timeline only, so call `set_scope` with no nest first.
194	- `content` is empty.
195	- No clip of a video file or a picture, with its video on, plays at `at` on a shown track that isn't a matte track.
196	- The named clip isn't a clip of a video file or a picture, with its video on, on a shown track that isn't a matte track.
197	- The named clip doesn't play at `at`.
198	
199	To put any other drawing clip behind the subject by hand, use `set_video` with [`behind_subject`](/mcp/tools-set-video/). An adjustment or nest clip can't take it.

212	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
213	
214	An [action](/motion/actions/) is a span on a clip over which its properties ease from what they are to an end state. These tools add one, say what it ends at, change its timing and take it away.
215	
216	<AtAGlance
217	  tools={['add_action', 'add_zoom_action', 'set_action', 'set_action_end', 'remove_action']}
218	  menu="Clip ▸ Add Action"
219	  keys="⌥⌘K"
220	  where="Clip tab ▸ action lane"
221	/>
222	
223	The usual order is two calls. First, `add_action` with these arguments:
224	
225	```json
226	{ "clip": 12, "at": 600000, "duration": 1200000 }
227	```
228	
229	Then `set_action_end`, with the id it answered in `new_actions`:
230	
231	```json
232	{ "clip": 12, "action": 40, "patch": { "video": { "scale": 1.4 } } }
233	```
234	
235	Every time here is in ticks, 600,000 to the second, and is rounded to the project's frame grid. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/). An action's times are clip time, measured from the clip's own start, not the timeline's. `get_project` lists each clip's actions and their ids.
236	
237	For a speed ramp in one step, see `add_speed_ramp` on [Tools: speed and time](/mcp/tools-speed/).

239	## `add_action`
240	
241	Adds an action to a clip. Its end state starts empty, so nothing changes until `set_action_end` fills it in. It mirrors **Clip ▸ Add Action** (<kbd>⌥⌘K</kbd>) and the **+** button in the Clip tab's action lane. See [Add an action](/motion/add-an-action/).
242	
243	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
244	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
245	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip's id. |
246	| `at` | integer | Yes | Where the action starts, in clip time. |
247	| `duration` | integer | No | How long it runs. The default is 1 s (600,000). |
248	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest id, to edit inside that nest. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
249	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
250	
251	**What it answers.** `ok`, `clip`, `new_actions` (a list holding the new action's id) and the `project` summary. A new action's curve is `linear`. Use `set_action` to change it.
252	
253	**When it refuses.**
254	
255	- It would overlap another action on the clip, or run past the clip's end. Both sentences give the times involved.
256	- A negative `at` or a `duration` that isn't positive is an error.
257	
258	## `add_zoom_action`
259	
260	Adds an action that zooms the picture to a rectangle, the screencast zoom, or back out to the clip's own framing. It mirrors the canvas's Z mode and the **Zoom to Region** and **Zoom Back** buttons in the Clip tab's action lane. See [Zoom to Region](/motion/zoom-to-region/).
261	
262	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
263	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
264	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip's id. |
265	| `at` | integer | Yes | Where the zoom starts, in clip time. |
266	| `region` | object or null | Yes | The rectangle to zoom to, as `{x, y, width, height}`. `null` zooms back to the clip's own scale and position. |
267	| `duration` | integer | No | How long it runs. The default is 1 s (600,000). |
268	| `fit` | string | No | `fit`, the default, shows the whole region. `fill` covers the whole canvas, cropping whatever the region's shape doesn't match. |
269	| `curve` | string | No | How the zoom eases: `linear`, `ease_in`, `ease_out` or `ease_in_out`. The default is `ease_in_out`. |
270	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest id, to edit inside that nest. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
271	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
272	
273	```json
274	{ "clip": 12, "at": 0, "region": { "x": -320, "y": 180, "width": 640, "height": 360 } }
275	```
276	
277	`region` is in source pixels. `x` and `y` are its centre, measured from the centre of the clip's cropped picture, and `width` and `height` are its size. All four are required, and the key itself is required, so a forgotten rectangle can't turn into a zoom back.
278	
279	Over the action, the clip's `scale`, `x` and `y` ease to the values that bring the region to the canvas, measured through the clip's rotation. Rotation and crop are read as they are at `at`. The scale is held to the largest a clip can take, with the position worked out from that, so a region too small to fill the canvas still lands centred.
280	
281	**What it answers.** As `add_action`. The action is an ordinary one, so `set_action_end` can add to what it animates.
282	
283	**When it refuses.**
284	
285	- It would overlap another action or run past the clip's end, as `add_action`.
286	- A clip with no picture is an error: "clip 7 has no video properties".
287	- A `width` or `height` that isn't above 0, or a member the region doesn't have, is an error naming it.
288	
289	## `set_action`
290	
291	Moves an action, changes its length or changes its easing curve. It mirrors the selected action's start, length and curve controls in the Clip tab's action lane, and dragging a band. See [Move, resize or remove an action](/motion/change-an-action/).
292	
293	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
294	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
295	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip's id. |
296	| `action` | integer | Yes | The action's id. |
297	| `start` | integer | No | The new start, in clip time. |
298	| `duration` | integer | No | The new length. |
299	| `curve` | string | No | How the values ease: `linear`, `ease_in`, `ease_out` or `ease_in_out`. |
300	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest id, to edit inside that nest. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
301	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
302	
303	Give at least one of `start`, `duration` and `curve`. Any you leave out keep their value.
304	
305	**What it answers.** `ok` and the `project` summary. When the action's end names a speed, captions on a Captions track wholly inside a clip with sound are re-timed in the same step: `captions_retimed` lists them, and `captions_removed` lists those whose speech it no longer plays. See [Captions follow a speed change](/speed/captions-and-speed/).
306	
307	**When it refuses.**
308	
309	- It would overlap another action on the clip.
310	- It would end past the clip's end and later than it ended before. An action a trim left past the clip's end can still be re-curved, moved earlier or shortened.
311	- On a speed action, it would make the clip read past the end of its media. The sentence names the latest clip end that fits.
312	- On a speed action of a linked clip, it would change the clip's speed: "clip 7 is linked to clip 8: Attach Audio before changing its speed or direction".
313	- With none of the three arguments, the call answers "set_action needs start, duration or curve."
314	
315	## `set_action_end`
316	
317	Sets what an action animates to. It mirrors every inspector field written while an action is selected. See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/) and [What an action can animate](/motion/what-can-animate/).
318	
319	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
320	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
321	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip's id. |
322	| `action` | integer | Yes | The action's id. |
323	| `patch` | object | Yes | The end state, with `video`, `audio`, `text` and `graphic` groups and a top-level `speed`. |
324	| `off` | array of strings | No | `"group.key"` paths to switch off at the end. See [Switching off at an end](#switching-off-at-an-end). |
325	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest id, to edit inside that nest. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
326	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
327	
328	```json
329	{ "clip": 12, "action": 40, "patch": { "video": { "opacity": 0 }, "audio": { "volume": 0.2 } } }
330	```
331	
332	The patch merges into the end state key by key, at every depth, so a one-key `shadow` keeps the rest of it. A key set to `null` is removed from the end state, so that property stops being animated, and a group set to `null` removes the whole group.
333	
334	The `video`, `audio` and `text` groups take the same keys as [`set_video`](/mcp/tools-set-video/), [`set_audio`](/mcp/tools-set-audio/) and [`set_text`](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/). A colour is four numbers here too, and it ramps in OKLab with straight alpha. So do the chroma key's three numbers.
335	
336	A bad key or value is refused by its path with the group in it, such as `video.filters[1].kind`. Values aren't range-checked, though: an animation can aim past what a stored property could hold.
337	
338	**Sound.** Every key the sound's effects read animates: `pan`, `mono`, `channels`, `eq`, `hum`, `noise_reduction`, `gate`, `leveller`, `de_esser`, `compressor`, `limiter` and `isolation`, beside `volume` and the fades.
339	
340	- Numbers ramp.
341	- A switch changes when the action ends: a group or an EQ slot turned on, `mono`, `channels`, an EQ slope, hum's frequency and harmonics, and the leveller's response.
342	- `isolation` ramps from 0 on a clip with none.
343	- `duck`, `keep_pitch`, the fade shapes and `voice` are stored but never animate.
344	
345	See [Animate sound with actions](/audio/animate-sound/).
346	
347	**What it answers.** `ok` and the `project` summary. With `speed` in the patch it can add the keys listed under [Speed in an action](#speed-in-an-action).
348	
349	**When it refuses.** These keys are errors, a `null` included:
350	
351	| Key | Why, and what to do instead |
352	| --- | --- |
353	| `video.motion` | It's a preset tied to the clip's two ends. Set it with `set_video`. |
354	| `video.hide_silent` | It isn't an animation target. Set it with `set_video`. |
355	| `text.words` | Word times belong to speech. Set them with `set_text`. |
356	| `video.cutout.subject`, `video.cutout.quality` | They're the clip's own. Set them with `set_video`. A cutout's `edge`, `feather` and `background` do animate. |
357	| Any `shape` key | Shapes can't be animated, so `shape` isn't a group here. |
358	
359	### Animating graphic props
360	
361	A graphic clip's props are a fourth group: `graphic: {props: {<key>: <value>}}`, keyed by what its module declares. It mirrors the Graphic sub-tab's **Properties** with an action selected. See [Animate graphic properties](/graphics/animate-properties/).
362	
363	```json
364	{ "clip": 18, "action": 44, "patch": { "graphic": { "props": { "accent": "#ff5500", "count": 96 } } } }
365	```
366	
367	- A value is checked as `set_graphic` checks it, minimum and maximum included, against the module as the project's graphics folder holds it now.
368	- A number ramps along the curve and arrives with decimals, so 64 to 129 is 96.5 halfway. A module that needs a whole number rounds it.
369	- A colour blends in OKLab, with straight alpha.
370	- A string, a boolean and an enum switch to the end's value when the action ends.
371	- An image prop switches when the action ends. `""` names no image there.
372	- A prop the clip holds no value for starts from the module's current default, written into the clip in the same undo step.
373	- `graphic.props.<key>: null` removes that prop from the end, and `graphic: null` removes the whole group.
374	
375	`get_project` shows `kinds` beside `props`. Frame Job writes that and ignores any you send, so an end you read back can be sent again.
376	
377	**When it refuses.**
378	
379	- A prop its module marks `animate: false` is refused. Set it with `set_graphic`.
380	- `name`, `width`, `height`, `in` and `length` are refused: an action animates `graphic.props` only.
381	- While the module is missing or doesn't compile, a value is refused, and `get_graphic` says why. A `null` still removes.
382	- On a clip that isn't a graphic: "clip 7 is not a graphic clip".
383	
384	### Speed in an action
385	
386	`speed`, a number beside the groups, is a media clip's rate. The clip ramps from the rate in force to it along the curve and holds it after, and it keeps its start and length, playing more or less source. It mirrors the Speed section's **Rate** with an action selected. See [Build a ramp by hand](/speed/build-a-ramp/).
387	
388	```json
389	{ "clip": 12, "action": 40, "patch": { "speed": 3 } }
390	```
391	
392	The rate is clamped to ×0.1–×1000, and `speed: null` removes it.
393	
394	Above ×12 the clip's audio is left out, and the call that takes it there answers with `audio_left_out` (the clip ids) and `audio_note`. Captions on a Captions track wholly inside a clip with sound are re-timed in the same step: `captions_retimed` lists them, and `captions_removed` lists those whose speech it no longer plays.
395	
396	**When it refuses.**
397	
398	- An end rate that would read past the end of the clip's media. The sentence names the largest end rate that fits, or, when none down to ×0.1 does, the latest clip end that fits at ×0.1.
399	- `speed: null` when the clip would then read past the end of its media. The sentence names the latest clip end that fits.
400	- A value that isn't a number or `null`, or a clip that isn't a media clip.
401	- A rate on a linked clip: "clip 7 is linked to clip 8: Attach Audio before changing its speed or direction".
402	
403	### Switching off at an end
404	
405	`off` turns an optional property off at the end of the action. The path is stored as a `null` in the end state, where a `null` in `patch` removes the key instead. So `off` means "this shadow goes away by the end", and a `null` in `patch` means "stop animating the shadow".
406	
407	```json
408	{ "clip": 12, "action": 40, "patch": {}, "off": ["video.shadow", "audio.eq.band_2"] }
409	```
410	
411	- A path is `"group.key"`, with a group of `video`, `audio` or `text` and one of its top-level keys, such as `video.shadow`, `text.width` or `audio.limiter`.
412	- One deeper path exists: `audio.eq.<slot>` switches that EQ slot off. The slots are `high_pass`, `low_shelf`, `band_1`, `band_2`, `band_3`, `high_shelf` and `low_pass`.
413	- Only optional keys can go off. A required key such as `video.opacity` is refused.
414	- A path can't also be named in `patch`.
415	- `graphic` paths are refused: name the value a prop ends at in `patch`.
416	- `video.cutout` is refused: `set_video` with `{cutout: null}` removes a cutout.
417	- `video.motion`, `video.hide_silent` and `text.words` are refused here too.
418	
419	## `remove_action`
420	
421	Removes an action. The clip keeps its base properties. It mirrors the action lane's trash button and <kbd>⌫</kbd> with an action selected. See [Move, resize or remove an action](/motion/change-an-action/).
422	
423	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
424	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
425	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip's id. |
426	| `action` | integer | Yes | The action's id. |
427	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest id, to edit inside that nest. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
428	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
429	
430	**What it answers.** `ok` and the `project` summary. When the action named a speed, captions are re-timed in the same step, with `captions_retimed` and `captions_removed` as for `set_action`.
431	
432	**When it refuses.**
433	
434	- Removing a speed action when the clip would then read past the end of its media. The sentence names the latest clip end that fits.
435	- Removing a speed action from a linked clip: "clip 7 is linked to clip 8: Attach Audio before changing its speed or direction".
436	- An action id the clip doesn't have is an error.

451	
452	A [transition](/motion/transitions/) plays across the overlap between a clip and the clip before it on the same track, and it belongs to the later clip. Its length is that overlap. These tools make the overlap, choose the transition, and set how it eases and sounds.
453	
454	<AtAGlance
455	  tools={['add_transition', 'set_transition', 'set_transition_duration', 'set_transition_style']}
456	  menu="Clip ▸ Transition ▸"
457	  where="Clip tab ▸ Transition section"
458	/>
459	
460	Start with `add_transition` at a hard cut. Use `set_transition` and `set_transition_duration` on clips that already overlap.
461	
462	Every time here is in ticks, 600,000 to the second. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/).
463	
464	The kinds are `cross_dissolve`, `fade_black`, `fade_white`, `push_left`, `push_right`, `push_up`, `push_down`, `wipe`, `slide`, `zoom`, `wipe_left`, `wipe_up` and `wipe_down`. See [Transition styles](/motion/transition-styles/).
465	
466	An adjustment clip can't take a transition or overlap another clip, so these tools refuse one, and `set_transition` with `kind: null` is the only call that goes through. Fade it with opacity instead. See [Adjustment clips](/color/adjustment-clips/).
467	
468	## `add_transition`
469	
470	Makes an overlap at the hard cut before a clip and puts a transition on it. It mirrors **Clip ▸ Transition ▸** on a clip that butts up against the one before it. See [Add or remove a transition](/motion/add-a-transition/).
471	
472	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
473	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
474	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The incoming clip's id. |
475	| `duration` | integer | Yes | The overlap you want. It can land shorter, but it's never refused for being too long. |
476	| `kind` | string | No | The transition. Left out, it's the clip's stored kind, else `cross_dissolve`. It can't be `null`: `set_transition` clears one. |
477	| `align` | string | No | Which side the overlap comes out of: `center`, the default, `before` or `after`. Ignored with `ripple`. |
478	| `ripple` | boolean or string | No | `true` makes the overlap by sliding the incoming clip and everything after it left, for two clips with no footage beyond the cut. The default is `false`. |
479	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest id, to edit inside that nest. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
480	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
481	
482	```json
483	{ "clip": 15, "duration": 600000, "kind": "fade_black" }
484	```
485	
486	**How the overlap is made.** It's built from material the two clips already have: the source before the incoming clip's in point, and after the outgoing clip's out point. Nothing else on the timeline moves, and the pair's outer edges stay where they were.
487	
488	| `align` | Where the overlap comes from |
489	| --- | --- |
490	| `center` | Half from each side. An odd frame goes to the incoming clip, and a side with nothing to give passes its share to the other. |
491	| `before` | All from the incoming clip's head. |
492	| `after` | All from the outgoing clip's tail. |
493	
494	`duration` rounds to the nearest frame. It's then held to each side's spare material, to the neighbours on the track and to the limit on how far two clips can overlap, so a request too long for the media lands shorter. A nest clip has no spare head, and its tail ends at the nest's own length.
495	
496	A stored transition keeps its curve and crossfade. A new one eases at both ends and crossfades its sound. The incoming clip's actions move with its new first frame, so a zoom stays on the source frame it was drawn over.
497	
498	**With `ripple: true`.** This is the sheet's **Shift Clips Left** button, for when neither clip has footage beyond the cut. No material is read and `align` is ignored. The incoming clip and every clip at or after the cut, on every unlocked track, slide left by `duration`, so the timeline gets that much shorter and no clip's source window changes.
499	
500	- The shift is capped at half the shorter of the two clips.
501	- It's also limited to the largest whole-frame shift that leaves every moved track within the overlap limit.
502	- A clip on another track pushed into its neighbour gets a `cross_dissolve`.
503	- Markers don't move.
504	
505	**What it answers.** `ok` and the `project` summary.
506	
507	**When it refuses.**
508	
509	- A `duration` that isn't positive once it's rounded to the frame grid is an error.
510	- A clip not at a hard cut is an error naming which of three: it's the first clip on its track, there's a gap before it, or it already overlaps a clip. For that last one, use `set_transition` or `set_transition_duration`.
511	- A cut with no room: the request clamps to nothing against the two clips' spare material, their neighbours and the overlap limit. The sentence suggests `ripple: true`.
512	- A track already outside the overlap limit is refused by that rule before anything is fitted.
513	- With `ripple`: an incoming clip on a locked track, or clips with no room to overlap by shifting.
514	
515	## `set_transition`
516	
517	Sets the transition into a clip, or removes it. It mirrors the **Kind** pop-up in the Clip tab's **Transition** section. See [The Transition section](/motion/transition-settings/).
518	
519	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
520	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
521	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip's id. |
522	| `kind` | string or null | Yes | The transition, or `null` to remove it. |
523	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest id, to edit inside that nest. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
524	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
525	
526	The transition's length is the clip's overlap with the one before it, so a clip with no overlap ignores it until it has one. Make an overlap with `move_clip` or `set_transition_duration`. Changing the kind keeps the transition's curve and crossfade. A new one eases at both ends and crossfades its sound.
527	
528	**What it answers.** `ok` and the `project` summary.
529	
530	**When it refuses.** A missing `kind`, or a value that isn't one of the thirteen or `null`, is an error listing them.
531	
532	## `set_transition_duration`
533	
534	Makes a transition last `duration` by moving the clip, so its overlap with the clip before it equals that. It mirrors the **Duration** field in the Clip tab's **Transition** section. See [The Transition section](/motion/transition-settings/).
535	
536	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
537	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
538	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip's id. |
539	| `duration` | integer | Yes | The overlap length, rounded to the frame grid. |
540	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest id, to edit inside that nest. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
541	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
542	
543	**What it answers.** `ok` and the `project` summary.
544	
545	**When it refuses.**
546	
547	- On a track's first clip, which has nothing to overlap.
548	- Past half the shorter clip, snapped down. The sentence names that limit in ticks.
549	- A `duration` that isn't positive is an error. To clear a transition, use `set_transition` with `kind: null`.
550	
551	## `set_transition_style`
552	
553	Sets how a transition is eased, whether it crossfades the two clips' sound, and the crossfade's shape. It mirrors the **Curve** pop-up, the **Crossfade Audio** checkbox and the **Crossfade Shape** pop-up in the Clip tab's **Transition** section. See [The Transition section](/motion/transition-settings/).
554	
555	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
556	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
557	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip's id. |
558	| `curve` | string | No | How the transition's progress is eased: `linear`, `ease_in`, `ease_out` or `ease_in_out`. |
559	| `audio` | boolean or string | No | Crossfades the two clips' sound across the overlap. |
560	| `audio_shape` | string | No | The crossfade's curve. See the table below. |
561	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest id, to edit inside that nest. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
562	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
563	
564	`audio` and `ripple` take `true` or `false`, or those words or `"1"` and `"0"` as strings.
565	
566	| `audio_shape` | The curve, over the eased progress p |
567	| --- | --- |
568	| `plus_3db` | The default, constant power: sine in, cosine out. It holds the level across two unrelated takes, where a straight-line pair dips 3 dB. |
569	| `linear` | p in, 1 − p out. |
570	| `s_curve` | A slow start and a slow finish. |
571	| `minus_3db` | A slow start, rising fastest at the end. |
572	
573	The outgoing clip takes the shape of 1 − p.
574	
575	A key you leave out keeps what's there, so changing the curve never touches the crossfade, and the other way round.
576	
577	The tool writes onto any clip, with or without an overlap. A stored transition on a clip with no overlap isn't drawn until there is one. A clip with no transition at all gets a `cross_dissolve` with the style applied.
578	
579	**What it answers.** `ok` and the `project` summary.
580	
581	**When it refuses.** With none of the three keys, the call is an error naming them.

3:description: How a transition works in Frame Job, as the overlap between two clips on a track, and the rules that decide where one can go.
8:A transition carries the picture and sound from one clip into the next. In Frame Job it isn't a separate object you drop on a cut. It's what plays wherever two clips on the same track overlap.
18:A transition plays across the overlap between two clips on the same track, and the overlap's length is the transition's duration. To make a transition longer, you make the overlap longer, by dragging or trimming a clip or by typing a [Duration](/motion/transition-settings/#duration).
28:The quickest transition is an overlap. When an edit leaves a clip overlapping the clip before it on the same track, and the later clip has no transition stored, Frame Job adds a Cross Dissolve. It's eased (**Ease In Out**) and crossfades the sound (**Crossfade Audio** on).
30:That holds however the overlap came about:
39:## The overlap rules
41:Two clips on a track may overlap only as a transition, and two rules limit how:
43:- A clip can overlap at most one neighbour on each side.
44:- An overlap can be at most half as long as the shorter of the two clips. A 4 s clip and a 10 s clip can overlap by up to 2 s.
53:See [How edits work](/editing/how-edits-work/#the-overlap-rule).
3:description: Blur a moving clip along its path, the way a camera's shutter would, and see where the blur applies and where a clip stays sharp.
38:A clip's [recorded cursor](/recording/cursor-settings/) streaks along its own path too, even when the clip stands still. The cursor's click ripples stay sharp.
68:## Where it stays sharp

Each strip is dimmed outside its range. Luma is unticked, with a dimmed strip and greyed-out fields. Below are Invert, Blur at 0%, the Pick from Canvas button and a ticked Show Selection."
45:It holds the three ranges, then **Invert**, **Blur**, [Pick from Canvas](/color/pick-from-canvas/) and [Show Selection](/color/show-selection/).
51:The section's header says what's set: the ranges that are on, then `inverted`, then the blur. For example, `hue · sat · inverted · blur 20%`. It reads `off` when nothing is set.
53:**Reset** appears once anything is set, as long as no action is selected. It turns all three ranges off, clears **Invert** and sets **Blur** to 0 %, as one undo step named **Qualifier**.
133:## Blur
135:**Blur** softens the selection, not the picture. On noisy footage a speckled selection turns clean, and the grade blends into its surroundings.
139:| **Blur** | 0 to 100 %, a slider and a field with presets at 0, 25, 50, 75 and 100 behind its chevron | 0 % |

## Where it stays sharp

These draw sharp whatever **Motion Blur** says, and the row keeps its value:

- A clip in a [transition](/motion/transitions/), for the frames of the overlap, and every clip inside a nest clip that's in one.
- A clip on a [matte track](/canvas/matte-tracks/), and the clips a matte cuts.
- A clip cut by [Text Behind Subject](/effects/text-behind-subject/), and the copy of the person it draws.
- A clip with a [drop shadow](/effects/shadow/).
- A nest clip itself. The blur goes on the clips inside it. See [Nests and adjustment clips](#nests-and-adjustment-clips).

## Nests and adjustment clips

A nest clip can't take motion blur, so the row is greyed for it, and for any selection with a nest clip in it. Set the blur on the clips inside the nest instead. They blur when the nest moves.

title: What a call answers
description: How to read a tool's answer. A landed edit, a call that changed nothing, a refusal, an error, what a cloud tool says with no key, and which tools never touch the network.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A call tells you what happened in its answer, in words a model can act on. An edit lands, changes nothing, is refused, or is an error, and each reads differently.

<AtAGlance
  tools={['transcribe', 'transcribe_for_fillers', 'get_media_analysis', 'get_transcript', 'get_timeline_transcript', 'detect_fillers', 'detect_silence', 'split_at_shots', 'analyze_cutout']}
  needs="Your AssemblyAI key, only for a tool that sends to AssemblyAI."
/>

## Answers come back as tool results

Every answer comes back as the tool's result, so a model can read it and correct itself. A refused or invalid call is an ordinary tool result with `isError: true`, and its text is the message. It isn't a transport or JSON-RPC error. A call that changed nothing is marked the same way, and its message says the project is already in that state.

JSON-RPC errors are for the protocol itself. An MCP method the server doesn't know gets "method not found", and a `tools/call` with no tool name is an error too. A tool name that doesn't exist is an ordinary result: "Unknown tool: *name*".

| The answer | `isError` | Undo step | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [A landed edit](#a-landed-edit) | false | One | Read the ids and carry on |

anchors = json.loads((SCRATCH / "anchors/mcp-8.json").read_text())

    h = re.sub(r"[^\w\- ]", "", h)
    return h.replace(" ", "-")
